item.title: Sinkhole reopening, 8th November
item.description:
The road is starting to collapse again into a sinkhole - on the surface it looks like a puddle but this has previously (and might be already) opened up into a big hole due to the culverted stream that runs under the road here. It is possible to see the tarmac heaving.

item.title: Uneven and damaged pavement between 149 and 151 athenlay riad se15 3ej, 8th November
item.description:
There are several damaged pavement slabs that are broken and has raised out of position aswell as dipping this has been here for over 3 months. There is about approximately 2/3 cm dip where it joins onto an existing drop kerb entry onto a neighbour's driveway. item.title: Issue reported on 11/5/2024 has not been resolved, 8th November
item.description:
The street cherry tree on the grass verge outside my house has continued to lift the tarmac in the public path to 5cm. The crack in my wall as a result of the Council's street tree has lifted my wall by 2cm causing the crack it has generated to widen. I have previously requested that either the tree is removed or a root barrier is installed to protect my wall and ultimately my property. This has not been done and I cannot understand why the Council is happy to let the tree damage my property even more as time goes on.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 27, Hurstwood Avenue, Albany Park, Greater London
